result:
Nothing in `ces-revisions` produces a result yet, and there is no spec. The brief and the three research reports are background, so I'm staging this as a new project. Before I write any roadmap text, here are the candidate outcomes, tracks and costs.

## Candidate outcomes (unranked)

All candidates come from `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md` §C unless marked otherwise. Parts A and B of the brief are already answered by the three reports, so they are not outcomes.

| # | Outcome | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision size by stage over time for total nonfarm, SA, on real vintages: first→second, second→third, third→benchmark | Small data volume: about 45 years × 12 months × a few vintages. The real limit is how far back the archives go, which I haven't checked. |
| O2 | A news-versus-noise split of the two sample-based revision stages for total nonfarm, using a latent true path | Fit time can only be measured by running it. |
| O3 | How big the benchmark revisions are, with the March benchmark treated as an irregular, more precise observation and wedge-back spread across the months in between | About 40 benchmark events in total. Few data points, so expect wide uncertainty. |
| O4 | SA one- and two-month revisions split into a seasonal-factor part and an NSA-sample part, using NSA and SA vintages together | Depends on how many NSA vintages are archived, which I haven't checked. The ChatGPT report says nobody has published a long-run version of this split. |
| O5 | Effect of collection interval and first-closing rate on the size of one- and two-month revisions | Collection days can be computed from release dates. Closing rates come from published BLS tables; I haven't checked how far back they go. |
| O6 | Effect of appropriations, staffing and sample size on revision size, with shrinkage and an honest account of what can't be identified | Mostly your time: covariates built by hand from roughly 37 years of budget justifications plus FedScope. Days, not hours. |
| O7 | Partial pooling of driver effects across NAICS supersectors | About 11× the series of O1. Fit cost scales with that; only running it can tell. |
| O8 | One joint multi-stage model across all four stages, with Student-t errors and stochastic volatility, from the brief's full §C design | Only running it can tell. It is the most expensive fit by far. |

## Proposed tracks

- **A: Descriptive revision history (O1).** Known progression: get the vintages, compute revisions by stage, report how their size changes over time. Every other track uses its vintage panel.
- **B: Calendar and collection (O5).** Research.
- **C: Seasonal factors versus sample (O4).** Research.
- **D: Benchmark and wedge-back (O3, O7).** Research. Supersector pooling sits here because birth–death and benchmark error differ most by sector.
- **E: Institutional capacity (O6).** Research.
- **F: Joint model (O2, O8).** Research.

**Why the brief's single model is split into tracks:** whether collection days drive one-month revision size (B) and whether funding or staffing do (E) are separate questions. Either answer stands without the other, even though both explain revision size. In one model, B's answer, which varies sharply within each year and is likely well identified, would wait on E's hand-built and weakly identified covariates. The same reasoning separates C and D. F rejoins them once the parts have run on real data.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), uv, pytest and ruff.
- NumPyro for the full model, Dynamax where the latent state can be marginalized, Blackjax only if a custom kernel is needed, ArviZ for diagnostics, Polars for the vintage panel (from the brief).
- Units: thousands of jobs (from the brief).

**Proposed roadmap name:** `ces-revisions`, which would be written to `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file with that name exists.

**Proposed probe** (only if you say yes): read the data-availability section of the ChatGPT report (§3.3) and run one ALFRED query for PAYEMS and PAYNSA vintage depth. That would turn the "haven't checked" cost notes into figures. I've read only the opening 3,000 characters of each report so far.

## One request

Please rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks against each other. Then confirm or change the tracks, their kinds and the name, and tell me whether to run the probe.
